docstring:
Are there infinitely many $q$ for which there is a set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$,
$|A| = (\sqrt{2} + o(1))q^{1/2}$, with $A + A = \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$? [Gr24]
references: [CaHa20] Caprace, Pierre-Emmanuel, and Pierre de la Harpe. "Groups with irreducibly unfaithful subsets for unitary representations." Confluentes Mathematici 12.1 (2020): 31-68.
[CrLe07] Croot, Ernie, and Vsevolod F. Lev. "Open problems in additive combinatorics." Additive combinatorics 43.207-233 (2007): 1.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ᶠ (q : ℕ+) in Filter.atTop, ∃ A, A + A = Finset.univ ∧ |↑A.card / √↑↑q - √2| < ε
